task_read: A very long-horizon, multi-component build: a full Excel-clone product (HTTP server, persistence, SPA, JSON+WebSocket API, a large formula engine with dynamic arrays/spilling/iterative calc/goal-seek, XLSX round-tripping, pivots, conditional formatting, locale input, collaboration). The wire contract is deliberately underspecified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing first-party client (/dev_tests/helpers.py); grading is on a hidden suite far larger than the provided smoke tests, against LibreOffice ground truth. Feature breadth vastly exceeds what can be built perfectly in any session, so a skilled practitioner would invest heavily in orientation, decomposition, self-built verification, and continuous triage — this is near the ceiling of meta-work demand.

dimensions.name: Contract reverse-engineering & Excel-semantics grounding
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and grounding function/error behavior in real Excel-365 semantics before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly defers the wire shape to what helpers.py already calls, and grading uses a hidden suite plus LibreOffice ground truth. An agent that guesses shapes or invents semantics will fail broadly regardless of code quality; reading the client and probing the environment is the single highest-leverage act here.

anchors.0: Starts coding server/endpoints without reading helpers.py or run.sh; invents request/response shapes and function behavior from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once, grabs a couple of endpoint shapes, but leaves the cell `kind` discriminator, spill fields, and listing envelope guessed; no grounding in Excel edge-case semantics.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py to derive the core cell/patch/listing shapes and runs the smoke suite to see current state; consults Excel behavior for the common functions being implemented.
anchors.8: Systematically mines helpers.py for every shape it touches (spill anchors/ghosts, error sentinels, fill/sort/filter/pivot/collab bodies), cross-checks against run.sh, and deliberately resolves ambiguous Excel semantics (criteria wildcards, spill materialization, LWW ordering, iterative fixed-point) by reasoning or targeted probes before committing.
anchors.10: Builds and maintains a precise internal model of the entire contract traced to concrete client call sites, proactively surfaces underspecified corners (locale canonicalization, XLSX openpyxl constraints, ghost-write rejection), and re-probes the client/environment whenever a new subsystem is entered rather than assuming — orientation is continuous and evidence-anchored throughout.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & sequenced milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking a sprawling product into an ordered hierarchy of subsystems (core CRUD+persistence+health, recompute engine, functions, dynamic arrays, analyst surface, collab, XLSX, SPA) each with an explicit done-check and a dependency-aware order.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface spans dozens of loosely coupled features with hard dependencies (e.g. recompute engine underpins everything; spilling underpins dynamic arrays; XLSX/pivot depend on the cell model). Without deliberate sequencing an agent thrashes across half-built subsystems and lands nothing verifiable.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between random features (a distribution function here, a WebSocket handler there) with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat undifferentiated to-do of feature names with no dependency ordering and no notion of when each is 'done'.
anchors.5: Identifies major subsystems and tackles a sensible foundational order (server/health/persistence, then a working cell+recompute core, then functions), with rough per-milestone success signals.
anchors.8: A dependency-aware milestone plan where each milestone has a concrete acceptance check (endpoint returns X, run.sh subset green, spill materializes), foundations sequenced before dependents, and the plan reflects that the engine/spill core gates most later work.
anchors.10: A crisp, layered milestone hierarchy that sequences the whole build for maximum verified coverage, explicitly ordering by both dependency and grading payoff, with each milestone independently demonstrable — and the structure is revisited and re-ordered as understanding of the contract deepens.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — running run.sh, adding targeted tests, cross-checking against Excel/LibreOffice values, verifying XLSX via openpyxl, exercising performance bounds — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive provided tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec warns the dev_tests are a small smoke suite and grading is a much larger hidden suite against held-out ground truth. Passing run.sh proves almost nothing; only agent-designed verification (value correctness, round-trips, error mapping, perf thresholds) predicts hidden-suite success.

anchors.0: Never runs the tests or the server against real requests; assumes code works because it was written.
anchors.3: Runs run.sh and treats green as done; no checks for the many behaviors the smoke suite doesn't cover.
anchors.5: Runs run.sh plus some ad-hoc manual API calls to sanity-check the features built, catching obvious breakage.
anchors.8: Designs verification targeted at hidden-suite risk: checks formula values against known Excel results, verifies error-sentinel/HTTP-status mapping, round-trips CSV/XLSX (re-reading with openpyxl), exercises spill/ghost rejection and collab ordering, and checks at least one performance scenario against its threshold.
anchors.10: Establishes a reusable verification harness spanning subsystems (value oracles, round-trip diffs, perf timing, restart-persistence checks) run repeatedly as the build grows, treats any divergence from Excel/LibreOffice semantics as a failing signal to chase, and calibrates confidence per subsystem from evidence rather than assumption.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the feature surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which of the many subsystems/functions are done, working, or broken, and detecting when effort is stuck or circling on one area at the expense of the whole.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With this many features and a long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot — over-polishing one function family while whole subsystems remain unbuilt, or re-debugging the same recompute bug in circles. Accurate done-vs-remaining tracking is what sustains forward progress.

anchors.0: No sense of overall state; cannot say what's built vs pending; repeats the same fix attempts without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; discovers late that major subsystems were never started or silently regressed.
anchors.5: Keeps a running list of completed vs remaining subsystems and generally knows current status, though staleness or gaps creep in.
anchors.8: Maintains an accurate, updated ledger of subsystem status tied to verification results, notices when a subsystem is consuming disproportionate time, and catches regressions in previously-working areas.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise, evidence-backed picture of the whole surface across the entire horizon, proactively detects stuck/circular states early and names them, and uses the status picture to reallocate attention deliberately rather than drifting.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on divergence
dimensions.description: Revising design, approach, or plan when reality contradicts assumptions — wrong wire shape, mismatched Excel semantics, performance blown, a library that can't round-trip — instead of pressing on with a falsified premise.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many assumptions here are likely wrong on first contact (guessed shapes, naive full-recompute that violates perf bounds, an XLSX library that drops conditional formatting). The ability to detect the falsification and re-architect rather than patch around it determines whether the system converges.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence (failing tests, timeouts, shape mismatches) and keeps building on the broken assumption.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with local hacks that paper over symptoms without revisiting the wrong underlying design.
anchors.5: When a test or check fails, diagnoses and fixes the real cause, adjusting the approach for that feature.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a foundational choice is wrong (e.g. recompute strategy can't meet perf, a library can't satisfy XLSX fidelity, an assumed shape is contradicted by helpers.py) and re-architects the affected layer deliberately, updating the plan accordingly.
anchors.10: Treats divergence as information: quickly isolates falsified assumptions, weighs re-design vs workaround explicitly, pivots decisively while protecting already-working subsystems, and folds the lesson back into the plan and verification so the same class of error is caught earlier.

dimensions.name: Scope allocation under breadth-exceeds-capacity
dimensions.description: Deliberately allocating finite effort across a feature surface too large to finish perfectly — choosing which functions/subsystems to fully implement, which to stub, and which to defer to maximize graded coverage.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The catalog (hundreds of functions plus collab, XLSX, pivots, locale, goal-seek) almost certainly exceeds what can be built flawlessly. A skilled agent explicitly triages for marginal payoff on the hidden suite rather than either perfecting one corner or spreading so thin that nothing is solid — a resource-allocation judgment distinct from mere ordering.

anchors.0: No triage: builds whatever comes to mind, commonly over-investing in a narrow area while leaving breadth untouched, or leaving core paths half-working.
anchors.3: Implicitly picks features by convenience with no reasoning about coverage or payoff.
anchors.5: Prioritizes clearly high-value, high-frequency features (core CRUD, common functions, spilling) before exotic ones, with rough awareness that not everything will be finished.
anchors.8: Makes explicit allocation decisions — securing broad correct coverage of common behavior first, consciously stubbing or deferring low-payoff exotica, and defending the choices in terms of hidden-suite value and remaining budget.
anchors.10: Continuously re-triages as budget burns and evidence accrues, trading depth for breadth (or vice versa) with explicit expected-value reasoning, ensuring the delivered system is broadly correct and coherent rather than a few polished islands amid unbuilt or broken subsystems.
